excerpts:
**The ads MCP server is a Meta-hosted [Model Context Protocol ⁠](l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmodelcontextprotocol.io%2F&h=AUDG75yalTyocickccUzIMH2cj_JZlNUjihkWxWREFyLCe0RF7IZGDnFQztiJ0o9Z02fPJUNxv1ucA3TZTdJjonr2_9-R4wkyhUwfN9mUhAerrHvYCHPG5YP0_H9zWpHn0NhW…) server** that lets you manage Meta ads directly from an AI agent. It is one of [Meta’s ads AI connectors ⁠](facebook.com/business/news/meta-ads-ai-connectors) — a family of integrations that expose Meta business surfaces to third-party AI clients through structured, permission-scoped tools.

The server is remote-hosted at `mcp.facebook.com/ads` and works with any MCP-compatible AI agent.

## Who it’s for

* **Advertisers using AI assistants** who want to manage Meta ads through a chat interface instead of Ads Manager or code
* **Developers building AI-native ad workflows** who want structured, permission-scoped access to ads capabilities without wiring up individual endpoints

## What the server can do

The server exposes tools grouped into seven categories:

|Category |What the server can do |
| --- | --- |
|[Comprehensive reporting](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-tools-comprehensive-reporting) |Gain valuable insights and pull detailed reporting to better understand campaign performance. |
|[Ad creation and management](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-tools-ad-creation-and-management) |Create and edit ads, ad sets, and campaigns. |
|[Catalog creation and management](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-tools-catalog-creation-and-management) |Create a catalog and add product data, and efficiently troubleshoot data feed and item visibility issues. |
|[Signals and datasets](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-tools-signals-and-datasets) |Access signal health and quality information, providing insights into where you should prioritize investment in your signals setup. |
|[Help and troubleshooting](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-tools-help-and-troubleshooting) |Execute a search of Meta Business Help Center articles relevant to a query. |
|[A/B tests and conversion lift studies](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-tools-abtests-and-conversion-lift-studies) |Create and manage A/B tests and conversion lift studies, and retrieve details on existing tests and studies. |
|[Activity logs](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-tools-activity-logs) |Get visibility into activity log changes for an ad account, mirroring the Ads Manager campaign history page. |

See Available tools for the full tool inventory by category.

# Authentication

Updated: Jun 24, 2026

Copy for LLM

[View as Markdown](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/get-started/authentication.md)

Ads in WhatsApp Status are available via the Marketing API. [Learn more about ads in WhatsApp Status.](developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/ads-in-whatsapp-status)

Every Marketing API call requires an access token as a parameter.

See [Access Tokens for Meta Technologies](developers.facebook.com/documentation/facebook-login/guides/access-tokens) for more information on the various types of access tokens.

## Get an access token for your app

### User access tokens

#### Graph API Explorer

You can get a user access token using the [Graph API Explorer](developers.facebook.com/tools/explorer) . To learn how to use the Graph API Explorer to make API calls, see the [Graph API Explorer Guide](developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/explorer) .

1. In the **Meta App** field, select an app to obtain the access token for.
2. In the **User or Page** field, select **User Token** .
3. In the **Add a Permission** drop-down under **Permissions** , select the permissions you need (for example, `ads_read` or `ads_management` ).
4. Click **Generate Access Token** . The box on top of the button displays the access token; store the token for later use.

#### Debug

To get more information in the token you just generated, click on the information icon ( **i** ) in front of the token to open the **Access Token Info** table, which displays some basic information about the token. Click **Open in Access Token Tool** to be redirected to the [Access Token Debugger](developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/accesstoken) .

While debugging, you can check:

* **App ID:** The app ID mentioned in the prerequisite section.
* **Expires:** A time stamp. A short-lived token expires in an hour or two.
* **Scopes:** Contains the permissions added in the Graph API Explorer.

#### Extend your access token

1. Paste your token in the text box of the [Access Token Debugger](developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/accesstoken) and click **Debug** .
2. Click **Extend Access Token** at the bottom of the **Access Token Info** table to get a long-lived token, and copy that token for later use.

Check your new token’s properties using the Access Token Debugger. It should have a longer expiration time, such as “60 days”, or “Never” under **Expires** . See [Long-Lived Access Token](developers.facebook.com/documentation/facebook-login/guides/access-tokens/get-long-lived) for more information.

### System user access tokens

A system user access token is a type of access token that is associated with a system user account, which is an account that is created in Meta Business Suite to manage assets and call the Marketing API. System user access tokens are useful for server-to-server interactions where there is no user present to authenticate. System user access tokens can be used to perform actions on behalf of the business, such as reading and writing business data, managing ad campaigns, and other ad objects.

One benefit of using a system user access token is that it does not expire, so it can be used in long-running scripts or services that need to access the Marketing API. Additionally, because system user accounts are not tied to a specific individual, they can be used to provide a level of separation between personal and business activity on Meta technologies.

System user tokens are also less likely to be invalidated than long-lived user access tokens.

See [System Users](developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/system-users) for more information.

## Get an access token for ad accounts you manage

After the owner of an ad account you are going to manage clicks the **Allow** button when you prompt for permissions, they are redirected to a URL that contains the value of the `redirect_uri` parameter and an authorization code:

```
```
YOUR_URL?code= < AUTHORIZATION_CODE >

...

You can then build the URL for an API call that includes the endpoint for getting a token, your app ID, your site URL, your app secret, and the authorization code you just received:

```
https : //graph.facebook.com/ v27.0 /oauth/access_token? 
  client_id =< YOUR_APP_ID > & redirect_uri =< YOUR_URL > & client_secret =< YOUR_APP_SECRET > & code =< AUTHORIZATION_CODE >
```

The API response should contain the generated access token:

System user access tokens can be used to perform actions on behalf of the business, such as reading and writing business data, managing ad campaigns, and other ad objects.
One benefit of using a system user access token is that it does not expire, so it can be used in long-running scripts or services that need to access the Marketing API. Additionally, because system user accounts are not tied to a specific individual, they can be used to provide a level of separation between personal and business activity on Meta technologies.
System user tokens are also less likely to be invalidated than long-lived user access tokens.
See System Users for more information.

Get an access token for ad accounts you manage

After the owner of an ad account you are going to manage clicks the Allow button when you prompt for permissions, they are redirected to a URL that contains the value of the redirect_uri parameter and an authorization code:
YOUR_URL?code= < AUTHORIZATION_CODE >
You can then build the URL for an API call that includes the endpoint for getting a token, your app ID, your site URL, your app secret, and the authorization code you just received:
https : //graph.facebook.com/ v26.0 /oauth/access_token? 
  client_id =< YOUR_APP_ID > & redirect_uri =< YOUR_URL > & client_secret =< YOUR_APP_SECRET > & code =< AUTHORIZATION_CODE >
The API response should contain the generated access token:
* If you follow the server-side authentication flow, you get a persistent token.
* If you follow the client-side authentication flow, you get a token with a finite validity period of about one to two hours. This short-lived token can be exchanged for a persistent token by calling the Graph API endpoint for Extending Tokens .
If a system user of a business invokes the API, you can use a system user access token .
You can debug the access token, check for expiration, and validate the permissions granted using the Access Token Debugger or the programmatic validation API .

Get started

Get started

...

Create or reuse a Meta developer app

1. Go to developers.facebook.com/apps and create a new app, or open an existing app.
2. Add the Create & manage ads with ads MCP server use case.

Authentication

The ads MCP server supports three authentication methods.

OAuth

The MCP client redirects you to the Facebook Login for Business dialog. You sign in with your Facebook account or your Meta Managed Account (MMA) and approve the requested permissions. No manual token setup is required.
Make sure your Meta developer app’s redirect URL is configured correspondingly with your choice of MCP client in the Facebook Login for Business settings.

User access token

To generate a user access token, use the Graph API Explorer or your own OAuth flow, requesting the permissions listed below.

System user access token

You can also use a system user access token to access the ads MCP server, for example for programmatic or server-to-server setups. See System Users for how to create a system user and generate a token, requesting the permissions listed below.
Note: Only Employee -role system user access tokens are supported. Admin-role system user access tokens can’t access the ads MCP server.

Permissions

These permissions apply to both user access tokens and system user access tokens.
At a minimum, the token must be granted:
* ads_mcp_management
* ads_read or ads_management
Granting additional permissions enables access to more tools:
* ads_management
* catalog_management
* business_management
* pages_show_list
* instagram_basic

Connect to ads MCP server

Sever URL of the ads MCP server
mcp.facebook.com/ads

Connect to the ads MCP server from Claude Code

To add the ads MCP server to Claude Code ⁠ , run the command below.
claude mcp add --transport http --client-id <META_APP_ID> meta-ads mcp.facebook.com/ads

Connect to the ads MCP server from ChatGPT

Set the redirect URL of your Meta developer app according to ChatGPT’s specification ⁠ .
Follow ChatGPT ⁠ instruction:
* Select “OAuth” as Authentication method
* Input mcp.facebook.com/ads as the Server URL
* In Advanced OAuth Settings, input your Meta developer app ID as the OAuth Client ID.

Connect to the ads MCP server with user access token

For programmatic setups, pass an user access token to in the request to the ads MCP server in the Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN> header.
curl -i -X POST "mcp.facebook.com/ads" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>" \
    --data-raw '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}'

results.title: Meta's ads MCP server is now available for developers
excerpts:
Home Blog Meta's ads MCP server is now available for developers
July 16, 2026

Meta's ads MCP server is now available for developers

By Sydney Levitan, Sanjay Patel

Updated September 22, 2026
Today, we are opening up our ads MCP server to any developer with their own Meta app. You can now connect your AI application directly to Meta's advertising capabilities, enabling your users to create and optimize campaigns, pull performance insights, manage product catalogs, and more through natural language. This means any developer can now bring Meta's ads MCP capabilities into the tools their customers already use — whether that's a marketing platform, a data warehouse, or a custom internal system.
Previously, connecting AI agents to Meta ads required writing and maintaining custom integration code. Now, developers can skip that entirely.

How do I connect using my own app?

1. Go to the developer dashboard and select the app you'd like to use.
2. Click Use cases in the left navigation, then Add use cases .
3. In the popup, click Ads and monetization , select Create & manage ads with ads MCP server , and click Save.
4. OPTIONAL If you manage data on behalf of other businesses, for example you are an agency or a partner, you need to submit your app for review.
* Request Advanced Access on the ads_mcp_management permission.
* On the 'Use cases' screen, click Customize for the ads MCP server use case.
* On the 'Permissions and features' tab, click Actions to get Advanced Access, then click Go to app review .
5. Choose how to authenticate: OAuth for automatic token handling via Facebook Login for Business, or pass a pre-obtained access token if you manage your own token lifecycle.

The Marketing API Access Tier controls your rate limits, Business Manager access, and system user capacity. Your tier is determined by whether your app has been approved through App Review.
*  | Limited access (default) | Full access (after App Review)

* Rate limits | Heavily rate-limited per ad account. For development only. Not for production apps running for live advertisers. | Lightly rate limited per ad account.
* Account limits | Manage an unlimited number of ad accounts. App admins or developers can make API calls on behalf of ad account admins or advertisers. | Manage an unlimited number of ad accounts, assuming you get ads_read or ads_management permission from the ad account.
* Business Manager | Limited access to Business Manager and Catalog APIs. No Business Manager access to manage ad accounts, user permissions, and Pages. | Access to all Business Manager and Catalog APIs.
* System users | Can create 1 system user and 1 admin system user. | Can create 10 system users and 1 admin system user.
* Page creation | Cannot create Pages through the API. | Cannot create Pages through the API.
To check your current access level, go to App Dashboard > App Review > Permissions and Features .

Permissions and Features

Permissions

The permissions you should request change depending on which API you want to access.
If your app is only managing your ad account, standard access to the ads_read and ads_management permissions are sufficient. If your app is managing other people’s ad accounts, you need advanced access to the ads_read and/or ads_management permissions. See all available permissions for business apps .

...

Get Full access

In order to get Full access of Marketing API Access Tier, your app needs to meet these requirements:
* Have successfully made at least 500 Marketing API calls in the last 15 days.
* Have made Marketing API calls with an error rate of less than 15% in the last 500 calls.
If you’re managing someone’s ads, use the scope parameter to prompt them for the ads_management or ads_read permissions. Your app gets access when they click Allow .
https : //www.facebook.com/ v25.0 /dialog/oauth? 
  client_id =< YOUR_APP_ID > & redirect_uri =< YOUR_URL > & scope = ads_management
Note: When inputting the YOUR_URL field, put a trailing / (for example, facebook.com/).

Example Use Cases

* Use Case | What To Request

Use this guide to connect a supported AI client to a remote Meta MCP server and authorize access with OAuth. When you finish, your client can discover and execute the server’s available tools.

Before you begin

To connect a client, you need:
* A current version of a supported AI client.
* A Meta account with access to the assets that the server manages. Assets are the businesses, apps, and accounts that you select when you grant consent.

...

Automatic registration uses OAuth dynamic client registration. The server recognizes the client during OAuth setup and returns its registered OAuth app identity. You don’t need to create a Meta app or provide an App ID.
Each server recognizes a specific set of clients. If a server doesn’t recognize yours, it declines automatic registration, and you need a developer-provided client ID instead.

Developer-provided client ID

Use a developer-provided client ID when the server-specific page requires one, or when the server doesn’t recognize your client. Follow that page’s instructions to create or configure a Meta app, including its redirect URI. Then use the app’s App ID as the OAuth client ID.
For example, connecting to the Meta Ads MCP server with your own Meta app uses this path. Its Get started page describes the app setup and redirect URL.
The Meta MCP servers listed on this site use OAuth public clients with Proof Key for Code Exchange. Don’t enter or share an App Secret.

Access Levels, Permissions, and Features

Business apps are subject to an additional layer of Graph API authorization called access levels . During App Review , your app must also request specific permissions and features.
All developers must follow all Meta Platform Terms and Developer Policies . Calls on ANY access level are against production data.

Marketing API Access Levels vs. Marketing API Access Tier

Permissions and features for apps have two different access levels: standard access and advanced access ( Note: The use of the term "standard access" here refers to platform-wide access levels and is not related to the Marketing API Access Tier , which has its own tiers: "Limited access" and "Full access".) To upgrade your Marketing API Access Tier, your app must meet the requirements shown in the App Dashboard.

Marketing API Access Tier overview

The Marketing API Access Tier controls your rate limits, Business Manager access, and system user capacity. Your tier is determined by whether your app has been approved through App Review.
*  | Limited access (default) | Full access (after App Review)
* How to get | Automatically granted when you add the Marketing API product to your app. | Click +Upgrade for the Marketing API Access Tier feature in your App Dashboard. Your app must meet the requirements below .
* Rate limits | Heavily rate-limited per ad account. For development only. Not for production apps running for live advertisers. | Lightly rate limited per ad account.
* Account limits | Manage an unlimited number of ad accounts. App admins or developers can make API calls on behalf of ad account admins or advertisers. | Manage an unlimited number of ad accounts, assuming you get ads_read or ads_management permission from the ad account.
* Business Manager | Limited access to Business Manager and Catalog APIs. No Business Manager access to manage ad accounts, user permissions, and Pages. | Access to all Business Manager and Catalog APIs.
* System users | Can create 1 system user and 1 admin system user. | Can create 10 system users and 1 admin system user.
* Page creation | Cannot create Pages through the API. | Cannot create Pages through the API.
To check your current access level, go to App Dashboard > App Review > Permissions and Features .

Permissions

The permissions you should request change depending on which API you want to access.
If your app is only managing your ad account, standard access to the ads_read and ads_management permissions are sufficient. sources.trimmed:
# Marketing API

The Marketing API is a collection of Graph API endpoints and other features that can be used to help you advertise across Meta technologies. Before advertising on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp, we recommend you learn about Meta's ad campaign structure to understand the objects you're working with and how they relate to each other.

Get started

Updated: Jun 24, 2026

Copy for LLM

View as Markdown

Ads in WhatsApp Status are available via the Marketing API. Learn more about ads in WhatsApp Status.

Every Marketing API call requires an access token as a parameter.

See Access Tokens for Meta Technologies for more information on the various types of access tokens.

## Get an access token for your app

### User access tokens

#### Graph API Explorer

You can get a user access token using the Graph API Explorer. To learn how to use the Graph API Explorer to make API calls, see the Graph API Explorer Guide.

1. In the **Meta App** field, select an app to obtain the access token for.
2. In the **User or Page** field, select **User Token**.
3. In the **Add a Permission** drop-down under **Permissions**, select the permissions you need (for example, `ads_read` or `ads_management`).
4. Click **Generate Access Token**. The box on top of the button displays the access token; store the token for later use.

#### Debug

To get more information in the token you just generated, click on the information icon (**i**) in front of the token to open the **Access Token Info** table, which displays some basic information about the token. Click **Open in Access Token Tool** to be redirected to the Access Token Debugger.

While debugging, you can check:

* **App ID:** The app ID mentioned in the prerequisite section.
* **Expires:** A time stamp. A short-lived token expires in an hour or two.
* **Scopes:** Contains the permissions added in the Graph API Explorer.

#### Extend your access token

1. Paste your token in the text box of the Access Token Debugger and click **Debug**.
2. Click **Extend Access Token** at the bottom of the **Access Token Info** table to get a long-lived token, and copy that token for later use.

Check your new token’s properties using the Access Token Debugger. It should have a longer expiration time, such as “60 days”, or “Never” under **Expires**. See Long-Lived Access Token for more information.

### System user access tokens

A system user access token is a type of access token that is associated with a system user account, which is an account that is created in Meta Business Suite to manage assets and call the Marketing API. System user access tokens are useful for server-to-server interactions where there is no user present to authenticate. System user access tokens can be used to perform actions on behalf of the business, such as reading and writing business data, managing ad campaigns, and other ad objects.

One benefit of using a system user access token is that it does not expire, so it can be used in long-running scripts or services that need to access the Marketing API. Additionally, because system user accounts are not tied to a specific individual, they can be used to provide a level of separation between personal and business activity on Meta technologies.

System user tokens are also less likely to be invalidated than long-lived user access tokens.

See System Users for more information.

## Get an access token for ad accounts you manage

After the owner of an ad account you are going to manage clicks the **Allow** button when you prompt for permissions, they are redirected to a URL that contains the value of the `redirect_uri` parameter and an authorization code:

```
```
http://YOUR_URL?code=<AUTHORIZATION_CODE>
```
```

You can then build the URL for an API call that includes the endpoint for getting a token, your app ID, your site URL, your app secret, and the authorization code you just received:

```
https://graph.facebook.com/v27.0/oauth/access_token?
  client_id=<YOUR_APP_ID>
  &redirect_uri=<YOUR_URL>
  &client_secret=<YOUR_APP_SECRET>
  &code=<AUTHORIZATION_CODE>
```

The API response should contain the generated access token:

* If you follow the server-side authentication flow, you get a persistent token.
* If you follow the client-side authentication flow, you get a token with a finite validity period of about one to tw

# Get started

Updated: Sep 4, 2026

Copy for LLM

View as Markdown

Owning a Meta app is not a prerequisite on using the ads MCP server. For access without owning a Meta app, follow How to set up Meta ads AI connectors⁠ instead.

To use the ads MCP server with your own Meta app, you must follow some key steps to set up your environment and gain access.

## Create or reuse a Meta developer app

1. Go to developers.facebook.com/apps and create a new app, or open an existing app.
2. Add the **Create & manage ads with ads MCP server** use case.

## Authentication

The ads MCP server supports three authentication methods.

### OAuth

The MCP client redirects you to the Facebook Login for Business dialog. You sign in with your Facebook account or your Meta Managed Account (MMA) and approve the requested permissions. No manual token setup is required.

Make sure your Meta developer app’s **redirect URL** is configured correspondingly with your choice of MCP client in the **Facebook Login for Business** settings.

### User access token

To generate a user access token, use the Graph API Explorer or your own OAuth flow, requesting the permissions listed below.

### System user access token

You can also use a system user access token to access the ads MCP server, for example for programmatic or server-to-server setups. See System Users for how to create a system user and generate a token, requesting the permissions listed below.

> **Note:** Only **Employee**-role system user access tokens are supported. Admin-role system user access tokens can’t access the ads MCP server.

### Permissions

These permissions apply to both user access tokens and system user access tokens.

At a minimum, the token must be granted:

* `ads_mcp_management`
* `ads_read` or `ads_management`

Granting additional permissions enables access to more tools:

* `ads_management`
* `catalog_management`
* `business_management`
* `pages_show_list`
* `instagram_basic`

## Connect to ads MCP server

Sever URL of the ads MCP server

```
https://mcp.facebook.com/ads
```

### Connect to the ads MCP server from Claude Code

To add the ads MCP server to Claude Code⁠, run the command below.

```
claude mcp add --transport http --client-id <META_APP_ID> meta-ads https://mcp.facebook.com/ads
```

### Connect to the ads MCP server from ChatGPT

Set the redirect URL of your Meta developer app according to ChatGPT’s specification⁠.

Follow ChatGPT⁠ instruction:

* Select “OAuth” as Authentication method
* Input https://mcp.facebook.com/ads as the Server URL
* In Advanced OAuth Settings, input your Meta developer app ID as the OAuth Client ID.

### Connect to the ads MCP server with user access token

For programmatic setups, pass an user access token to in the request to the ads MCP server in the `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>` header.

```
curl -i -X POST "https://mcp.facebook.com/ads" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>" \
    --data-raw '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}'
```

## Run your first prompts

Once connected, try:

* “List my ad accounts.”
* “Create a new traffic campaign in ad account `<AD_ACCOUNT_ID>`.”
* “Draft an ad set for my `<CAMPAIGN_ID>` campaign that optimizes for link clicks.”
* “Summarize the top-spending campaigns in `<AD_ACCOUNT_ID>` over the last 30 days.”

# Meta's ads MCP server is now available for developers

#### By Sydney Levitan, Sanjay Patel

*Updated September 22, 2026*

Today, we are opening up our ads MCP server to any developer with their own Meta app. You can now connect your AI application directly to Meta's advertising capabilities, enabling your users to create and optimize campaigns, pull performance insights, manage product catalogs, and more through natural language. This means any developer can now bring Meta's ads MCP capabilities into the tools their customers already use — whether that's a marketing platform, a data warehouse, or a custom internal system.

Previously, connecting AI agents to Meta ads required writing and maintaining custom integration code. Now, developers can skip that entirely.

## How do I connect using my own app?

1. Go to the developer dashboard and select the app you'd like to use.
2. Click **Use cases** in the left navigation, then **Add use cases**.
3. In the popup, click **Ads and monetization**, select **Create & manage ads with ads MCP server**, and click **Save.**
4. **OPTIONAL** If you manage data on behalf of other businesses, for example you are an agency or a partner, you need to submit your app for review.

   * Request Advanced Access on the *ads\_mcp\_management* permission.

     + On the 'Use cases' screen, click **Customize** for the ads MCP server use case.
     + On the 'Permissions and features' tab, click **Actions** to get Advanced Access, then click **Go to app review**.
5. Choose how to authenticate: OAuth for automatic token handling via Facebook Login for Business, or pass a pre-obtained access token if you manage your own token lifecycle.

## Managing agent controls programmatically

Connecting an agent to an ad account raises an obvious question: can you control what the agent does? Yes - via ads MCP server rules. Rules define the actions an AI agent can and cannot take on a given ad account or catalog. For example, you can grant an agent read access to performance data while withholding the ability to make changes to budgets, campaigns, or creative.

Until now, those rules could only be set one asset at a time in Meta Business Suite settings. That is workable for a single advertiser but impractical for users operating at scale.

**Rules are now available through the Marketing API**. A new endpoint lets you set and manage agent controls in bulk, across many ad accounts and catalogs at once. For developers, this moves guardrail configuration out of manual setup and into your provisioning code. A few things that become possible:

* **Configure controls at onboarding**. When a new advertiser or client account connects to your application, apply your permission model as part of the same automated flow — no manual step in Ads Manager, and no gap between connection and correct guardrails.
* **Enforce a policy consistently across a portfolio**. Define one control posture and apply it to every account you manage, rather than relying on per-account configuration staying correct over time.
* **Offer controls as a product surface**. Expose your own permission settings to your users and translate them into ads MCP server rules underneath, so agent boundaries become something your customers configure in your interface.
* **Adjust as trust develops**. Start an account in a read-only or approval-required posture and widen permissions programmatically as confidence grows, instead of treating access as a one-time decision.

**Availability**. The endpoint matches current rules availability: any ad account with access to ads MCP server rules in Ads Manager can also be managed through the API. If an account can be configured in Ads Manager today, it can be configured programmatically.

Setup detail, supported rule types, and recommended configurations are in the ads MCP server rules best practices guide.

## What can you do with Meta's ads MCP server
